answer: Let reputation ride a tide: marks accrue only during short, unpredictable high-tide windows when fresh useful work is demanded, and each mark washes away after one season unless renewed by new work. To survive the tundra season, a long quiet stretch with no new marks issued, an identity must hold marks from several past seasons, sealed in a sable ledger nobody can rewrite. A farm cannot stockpile marks for clones, since windows are brief, marks expire, and every clone must earn its own seasons one by one; multiplying accounts multiplies waiting, not reward.
